residual_risks: Shutdown now waits on admitMu before close(b.closed). If a Commit is parked on `b.in <-` (buffer full while commitLoop is inside a slow commitBatch), Shutdown and every later Commit queue on the mutex. During that window new Commits are admitted rather than rejected with 'batcher is shutting down', so Ctrl-C/atexit shutdown can take longer under a saturated batcher. Not a deadlock, because commitLoop keeps draining b.in and the old code also blocked on `b.in <- quit` when full. It is a small behavioural shift with bounded impact.

If commitLoop ever dies (for example the user commit function panics), a Commit parked on `b.in <-` now holds admitMu forever and wedges all other Commits and Shutdown on the mutex, instead of only itself. The old code hung the same senders on the channel, so the outcome is equivalent and only reachable after a panic.

callsite completeness: grep-only. Commit/Shutdown callers in backend/dropbox (dropbox.go:2122, 1763) and backend/googlephotos (googlephotos.go:1226, 891) call them without holding other locks and not from inside commitBatch. No lock-order inversion with admitMu was found.
